question: Do real CartPole action-consequence training episodes yield a reproducible stronger factual token-free history policy than a near-matched nonrecurrent history model and a strong observation-feedback conventional controller?
null: Original real-world factual DEV reward-trained GRU does not beat equally updated history-MLP by >=10 steps, transparent state-feedback champion by >=10 steps, same-init untrained GRU by >=10, and history-corrupted negative by >=5 steps in each of three init seeds. No first-use science claim.

design.environment: Farama Gymnasium CartPole-v1 exact pinned source v1.1.1, no CausalGym wind
design.engine_observations_used: ONLY four public floating observation coordinates from reset/step, two discrete real actions, factual real reward, termination/truncation; no environment.state/engine parameters/hidden wind
design.actor_history_features: 4 current public observation plus PRIOR executed actual action coded ±1 and its completed observed reward; 6 floating values per time row; padded initial history
design.model_training: REINFORCE discounted factual reward-to-go gamma .99 with trained value head smooth_l1 factor .5, entropy 0.01, AdamW LR .003, clip3, one actual gradient update per completed episode
design.training_env_reset_seeds: 51000..51063 independent public DEV, every trained arm same reset sequence; no protected science seeds
design.strong_conventional: Obvious observation-based CartPole balancing stabilizer: action=sign(theta+0.5*theta_dot), no latent engine state; no oracle access, no matched training compute
design.negative_history: reverse previous seven completed factual input rows but preserve current sensor row, trained GRU weights unchanged
design.negative_untrained: same original initialized GRU weights before all actual optimizer updates
design.negative_random: seeded random decisions, same actual reset observation
